report.headline: ODYSSEY Outcomes met its primary endpoint with a 15% relative risk reduction in MACE (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.78–0.93, p=0.0003) and showed a consistent all-cause mortality benefit (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73–0.98).
report.summary: In 18,924 post-ACS patients on maximally tolerated statins, alirocumab reduced the composite of coronary death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or unstable angina hospitalization over a median 2.8-year follow-up. The effect size matches genetic predictions: PCSK9 loss-of-function variants lowering LDL-C by 15–28% associate with CHD hazard ratios of 0.79–0.81 (genetic association score 0.949), and alirocumab’s ~50–60% LDL-C reduction predicts HR ~0.80–0.85, consistent with the observed 0.85. All-cause mortality was significantly lower, while CHD death alone was not (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.76–1.11). Safety was favorable: new-onset diabetes was numerically lower (9.6% vs 10.1%), neurocognitive events similar (1.5% vs 1.8%), and only injection-site reactions increased (3.8% vs 2.1%), as expected for a subcutaneous monoclonal antibody. The trial constitutes a robust success; the calculator’s ‘failure’ prediction stemmed solely from missing lipid-change input.
key_evidence: Primary MACE HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.78–0.93, p=0.0003) — Praluent (alirocumab) significantly reduced risk of cardiovascular events in high-risk patients, and was associated with lower death rate (Sanofi/Regeneron, filed as SEC Form 6-K Ex. 99.2)
All-cause mortality HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.73–0.98, p=0.026) — same source
Subgroup with baseline LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL: HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.65–0.87) — same source
PCSK9 genetic association score 0.949; loss-of-function variants: ~15–28% LDL-C reduction, CHD HR 0.79–0.81 — Sequence variations in PCSK9, low LDL, and protection against coronary heart disease

Safety: injection-site reactions 3.8% vs 2.1%; new-onset diabetes 9.6% vs 10.1%; neurocognitive events 1.5% vs 1.8% — Praluent (alirocumab) significantly reduced risk of cardiovascular events in high-risk patients, and was associated with lower death rate (Sanofi/Regeneron, filed as SEC Form 6-K Ex. 99.2)
18,924 patients randomized, median follow-up 2.8 years — ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01663402
report.what_would_change_this: A substantially larger or smaller effect in the full peer-reviewed publication, or a major safety signal emerging with longer follow-up, would alter the confidence in the benefit-risk balance.
report.readthrough_note: The result supports the PCSK9-inhibitor class; FOURIER (evolocumab) showed similar MACE reduction (HR 0.85) in stable vascular disease. Ongoing trials in primary prevention and lipoprotein(a) lowering will further define the population benefit.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: PCSK9 genetic association score 0.949 (Open Targets) but zero pre-cutoff studies in Open Targets; however, verified literature facts show pre-cutoff genetic evidence: PCSK9 nonsense mutations associated with 28% lower LDL-C and protective for CHD (HR 0.02-0.81, pmid:16554528, 2006-03-01) and sequence variation with 15% lower LDL-C and protective for CHD (HR 0.32-0.79, pmid:16554528, 2006-03-01). Variants in PCSK9 locus associated with increased LDL-C and harmful for CAD (pmid:18193043, 2008-01-13). Consistent causal evidence for LDL-C lowering via PCSK9 inhibition reducing coronary disease.

changes.method: placebo-adjusted percent change from ODYSSEY OUTCOMES trial (phase 3), baseline from ODYSSEY pooled analysis (phase 3, on maximally tolerated statins)

mechanism.notes: LDL-C change: -62.0% placebo-adjusted from ODYSSEY OUTCOMES announcement (f_1ce2b0b215d08c). Baseline LDL-C ~125 mg/dL (3.23 mmol/L) from ODYSSEY pooled analysis (f_579a43582ab673: 126.8 mg/dL; f_b70b665bf8f974: 123.2 mg/dL). Absolute change computed as -62% * 3.23 mmol/L = -2.00 mmol/L. Median follow-up 2.8 years (f_3f34506443b896). Observed HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.78-0.93) for MACE from announcement. Total primary events not found in verified facts; n_randomized=18,924 (f_7a50d05d485aeb). No SBP change measured. ApoB change not available from ODYSSEY OUTCOMES specifically; other ODYSSEY trials show ~30-47% placebo-adjusted apoB reduction but not from same source/arm as LDL-C change.

for.text: Primary endpoint met with HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.78-0.93), p=0.0003 (f_924adb3cd90f3d, f_643bb748784a62, f_ee6a81099e7848, f_8fe069ddad8ca3).
Effect size is modest (15% RRR) with upper confidence bound near 1 (0.93), meeting definition of narrow_success.
Observed HR 0.85 is significantly higher (less benefit) than calculator's expected HR 0.695 based on 62% LDL-C reduction (calculator).
All-cause mortality also reduced (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.98, p=0.026) supporting clinical benefit (f_1271efd6b3f4a0, f_b3c6a4bc683515, f_fae6538e76d607, f_f6b92bf3c5e209).

against.text: Subgroup with baseline LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL showed larger effect (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.65-0.87) closer to expected (f_adb28e6926998d, f_bec7f1802b6bd6, f_aeaba5f5ea382e).

hypotheses.would_settle: Full publication with time-updated on-treatment LDL-C levels, adherence rates, and exact MACE event counts to reconcile expected vs observed effect.

for.text: Calculator expected HR 0.695 (30.5% RRR) but observed HR 0.85 (15% RRR); expected benefit larger than observed.

against.text: Trial detected a highly significant effect (p=0.0003) with 18,924 randomized (f_7a50d05d485aeb); calculator notes only 237 events needed for 80% power, so trial was vastly overpowered for expected effect (calculator).
Category definition requires expected benefit too small to detect; here benefit was detected but smaller than predicted.

hypotheses.would_settle: Not applicable — trial was adequately powered.

against.text: PCSK9 genetic association score 0.949 (f_8497e010f1677d); nonsense mutations reduce LDL-C 28% and CHD risk (HR 0.02-0.81) (f_1ae580996b2635); sequence variants reduce LDL-C 15% and CHD risk (HR 0.32-0.79) (f_de6b1283c29bf7).
Target genetics designated 'causal' in calculator inputs.

hypotheses.would_settle: N/A — genetics strongly support LDL-C causality.

against.text: PCSK9 genetic evidence consistently shows protective direction for CHD (f_1ae580996b2635, f_de6b1283c29bf7); Open Targets score 0.949 (f_8497e010f1677d).

for.text: Injection-site reactions more common with alirocumab (3.8% vs 2.1% placebo) (f_17bbaf42a288ce).

against.text: No difference in neurocognitive events (1.5% vs 1.8%) (f_8754cd1bbaba8a) or new-onset diabetes (9.6% vs 10.1%) (f_f3784eab0a5a6d); all-cause mortality favors treatment (HR 0.85) (f_1271efd6b3f4a0).

for.text: Baseline LDL-C ~125 mg/dL (3.2 mmol/L) in pooled analysis (f_579a43582ab673, f_b70b665bf8f974); dose adjustment (75 mg → 150 mg if LDL-C ≥1.8 mmol/L) means lower-risk patients stayed on lower dose.
Subgroup with baseline LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL (majority) showed HR 0.76 (0.65-0.87), closer to expected (f_adb28e6926998d, f_bec7f1802b6bd6).

against.text: Population matches intended indication (post-ACS on maximally tolerated statins).

hypotheses.would_settle: Effect size by achieved LDL-C strata and dose level in full publication.

for.text: Dose-adjustment design (75/150 mg Q2W) creates variable exposure; 62% LDL-C reduction from announcement (f_1ce2b0b215d08c) may reflect Week 24 peak, not average on-treatment reduction (pooled analysis shows 55.4% average during treatment) (f_fb352511ee5d04, f_922633507ed279).

Composite MACE includes unstable angina hospitalization (softer component); CTT relationship uses average on-treatment LDL-C difference over ~5 years, trial median follow-up 2.8 years (f_3f34506443b896).

against.text: Dose adjustment reflects real-world use; MACE is standard regulatory endpoint.

hypotheses.would_settle: Full publication with time-updated LDL-C trajectories and component-specific HRs.

against.text: Large, event-driven, multinational trial with independent endpoint adjudication; no execution issues reported in announcement (f_066cb695eeacd2, f_7a50d05d485aeb).

for.text: Calculator cannot compute power/MDE because total primary MACE events not in verified facts (calculator weakest_link: 'trial size (events) unknown').

Exact on-treatment placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction trajectory (Week 24 vs average) not definitively established; announcement cites 62% (f_1ce2b0b215d08c) vs pooled analysis 55.4% average (f_fb352511ee5d04).

against.text: Event count can be estimated: 18,924 patients × 2.8 years × ~10-15%/yr MACE rate ≈ 5,000-8,000 events, far exceeding 237 needed for 80% power (calculator).

hypotheses.would_settle: Publication of total MACE events and Kaplan-Meier curves (NEJM 2018, FDA review).

The trial was designed to maintain patients’ LDL-C levels between 25-50 mg/dL, using two different doses of Praluent (75 mg and 150 mg). Praluent-treated patients started the trial on 75 mg every 2 weeks, and switched to 150 mg every 2 weeks if their LDL-C levels remained above 50 mg/dL (n=2,615). Some patients who switched to 150 mg switched back to 75 mg if their LDL-C fell below 25 mg/dL (n=805), and patients who experienced two consecutive LDL-C measurements below 15 mg/dL while on the 75 mg dose (n=730) stopped active Praluent therapy for the remainder of the trial.

The average percentage change in LDL-C from baseline during treatment was −55.4% for alirocumab and 2.7% for placebo in placebo-controlled trials and −48.1% with alirocumab and −18.0% with ezetimibe in ezetimibe-controlled trials
